function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or directive that gives someone the power or responsibility to act on behalf of another party. It can take various forms depending on the context: | Context | What it means | Typical examples | |---------|---------------|------------------| | **Legal / Governance** | A written or verbal instruction from a principal (e.g., a shareholder, a client) to an agent (e.g., a lawyer, a trustee) to perform specific actions. | • A shareholder voting mandate to a proxy;
• A power‑of‑attorney document granting a lawyer authority to sign contracts. | | **Financial Services** | A standing instruction that authorizes a financial institution to execute recurring transactions (payments, investments, etc.) on behalf of a customer. | • Direct debit for utility bills;
• Automatic investment plans (SIP) in mutual funds. | | **Business / Partnerships** | An agreement between partners or between a partner and a client that defines the scope of work, responsibilities, and authority levels. | • A partnership contract specifying each partner’s duties;
• A client mandate outlining the services a consultant will deliver. | In short, a mandate is a *formal delegation of authority*—it tells the authorized party exactly what they’re allowed (or required) to do, often with conditions such as time limits, scope, or performance metrics.
